t: Feria Quinta infra Hebdomadam XVI post Octavam Pentecostes I. Septembris ~ IV. classis
Commemoratio  ad Laudes tantum: S. Gorgonii Martyris
tv: Feria Quinta infra Hebdomadam XVI post Octavam Pentecostes I. Septembris ~ IV. classis

b.88533859b0:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Iob
<r>Iob 6:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Respóndens autem Iob, dixit:
<n>2</n> Utinam appenderéntur peccáta mea, quibus iram mérui, et calámitas, quam pátior, in statéra.
<n>3</n> Quasi aréna maris hæc grávior apparéret, unde et verba mea dolóre sunt plena;
<n>4</n> Quia sagíttæ Dómini in me sunt, quarum indignátio ébibit spíritum meum, et terróres Dómini mílitant contra me.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si bona suscépimus de manu Dei, mala autem quare non sustineámus? Dóminus dedit, Dóminus ábstulit:
* Sicut Dómino plácuit, ita factum est: sit nomen Dómini benedíctum.
<r>℣.</r> Nudus egréssus sum de útero matris meæ et nudus revértar illuc.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut Dómino plácuit, ita factum est: sit nomen Dómini benedíctum.
b.4a9e92c56d:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Job
<r>Job 6:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> But Job answered, and said:
<n>2</n> O that my sins, whereby I have deserved wrath, and the calamity that I suffer, were weighed in a balance.
<n>3</n> As the sand of the sea this would appear heavier: therefore my words are full of sorrow:
<n>4</n> For the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> What shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? The Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away. As the Lord hath pleased, so hath it befallen. Blessed be the Name of the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither.
* The Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away. As the Lord hath pleased, so hath it befallen. Blessed be the Name of the Lord.
b.3dba663522:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad gáudia paradísi perdúcat nos misericórdia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Iob 6:5-7</r>
<n>5</n> Numquid rúgiet ónager, cum habúerit herbam? aut múgiet bos, cum ante præsépe plenum stéterit?
<n>6</n> Aut póterit cómedi insúlsum, quod non est sale condítum? aut potest áliquis gustáre, quod gustátum affert mortem?
<n>7</n> Quæ prius nolébat tángere ánima mea, nunc præ angústia, cibi mei sunt.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Antequam cómedam, suspíro, et tamquam inundántes aquæ sic rugítus meus; quia timor, quem timébam, evénit mihi, et quod verébar áccidit. Nonne dissimulávi? nonne sílui? nonne quiévi?
* Et venit super me indignátio tua, Dómine.
<r>℣.</r> Ecce non est auxílium mihi in me, et necessárii quoque mei recessérunt a me.
<r>℟.</r> Et venit super me indignátio tua, Dómine.
b.fd03a57301:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Job 6:5-7</r>
<n>5</n> Will the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or will the ox low when he standeth before a full manger?
<n>6</n> Or can an unsavoury thing be eaten, that is not seasoned with salt? or can a man taste that which when tasted bringeth death?
<n>7</n> The things which before my soul would not touch, now, through anguish are my meats.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> My sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters, for the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me. Was not I silent? Held not I my peace? Was not I at rest?
* And trouble came.
<r>℣.</r> Behold, I cannot help myself, and they that were needful unto me have forsaken me.
<r>℟.</r> And trouble came.

<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>Iob 6:8-11</r>
<n>8</n> Quis det ut véniat petítio mea, et quod exspécto tríbuat mihi Deus?
<n>9</n> Et qui cœpit ipse me cónterat, solvat manum suam et succídat me?
<n>10</n> Et hæc mihi sit consolátio, ut afflígens me dolóre non parcat, nec contradícam sermónibus Sancti.
<n>11</n> Quæ est enim fortitúdo mea, ut sustíneam? aut quis finis meus, ut patiénter agam?
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Utinam appenderéntur peccáta mea, quibus iram mérui, et calámitas, quam pátior
* In statéra.
<r>℣.</r> Quasi aréna maris hæc grávior apparéret, unde et verba mea dolóre sunt plena.
<r>℟.</r> In statéra.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> In statéra.
b.f2c2f1ca04:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Job 6:8-11</r>
<n>8</n> Who will grant that my request may come: and that God may give me what I look for?
<n>9</n> And that he that hath begun may destroy me, that he may let loose his hand, and cut me off?
<n>10</n> And that this may be my comfort, that afflicting me with sorrow, he spare not, nor I contradict the words of the Holy One.
<n>11</n> For what is my strength, that I can hold out? or what is my end that I should keep patience?
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O that my sins, whereby I have deserved wrath;and the calamity whereunder I suffer, were laid in the balances together.
<r>℣.</r> For now it would appear heavier than the sand of the sea, therefore also my words are full of sorrow.
* And the calamity whereunder I suffer, were laid in the balances together.
b.5762da9658:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>T</c>ua nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátia semper et prævéniat et sequátur: ac bonis opéribus iúgiter præstet esse inténtos.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.1b83c8a27c:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>ord, we pray thee, that thy grace may always prevent and follow us, and make us continually to be given to all good works.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.24a589b3b6:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Idus Septémbris Luna nona. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>T</h>olentíni, in Picéno, deposítio sancti Nicolái Confessóris, ex Ordine Eremitárum sancti Augustíni.
<h>I</h>n Africa natális sanctórum Episcopórum Nemesiáni, Felícis, Lúcii, altérius item Felícis, Littéi, Polyáni, Victóris, Iadéris, Datívi et aliórum; qui, sub Valeriáno et Galliéno, exsurgénte persecutiónis rábie, ad primam confessiónis Christi constántiam gráviter fústibus cæsi sunt, deínde, compédibus vincti et ad fodiénda metálla deputáti, gloriósæ confessiónis agónem consummárunt.
<h>L</h>eódii, in Bélgio, sancti Theodárdi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui ánimam suam pósuit pro óvibus suis, et miraculórum signis post mortem illúxit.
<h>C</h>halcedóne sanctórum Mártyrum Sósthenis et Victóris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Asiæ Procónsule Prisco, post víncula et béstias superátas, iussi sunt incéndi; at illi, salutántes se ínvicem in ósculo sancto, in oratióne pósiti emisérunt spíritum.
<h>I</h>tem sanctórum Mártyrum Apéllii, Lucæ et Cleméntis.
<h>I</h>n Bithýnia sanctárum Vírginum sorórum Menodóræ, Metrodóræ et Nymphodóræ; quæ sub Maximiáno Imperatóre et Frontóne Prǽside, ob intrépidam in Christi fide constántiam martýrio coronátæ, pervenérunt ad glóriam.
<h>C</h>ompostéllæ sancti Petri Epíscopi, qui multis virtútibus et miráculis cláruit.
<h>I</h>n civitáte Albigénsi, in Gállia, sancti Sálvii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>N</h>ováriæ sancti Agápii Epíscopi.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctæ Pulchériæ Augústæ, Vírginis, religióne et pietáte insígnis.
<h>N</h>eápoli, in Campánia, sanctæ Cándidæ iunióris, miráculis claræ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.8531286312:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 10th 2027, the 9th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Tolentino, in the March of Ancona, the holy Confessor Nicholas, of the Order of Hermits of St Augustine.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy Bishops Nemesian, Felix, Lucius, another also named Felix, Litteus, Polyan, Victor, Jader, Dativus, and others, who, when the storm of persecution broke under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, at their first steadfastness in confessing Christ were heavily cudgelled, bound, and condemned to penal servitude in the mines, where they finished their glorious contending.
<h>A</h>t Liege, in Belgium, (in the seventh century,) the holy martyr Theodard, the Bishop, who laid down his life for the sheep, and shone with the grace of miracles after his death.
<h>A</h>t Chalcedon, the holy martyrs Sosthenes and Victor, who were condemned to be burnt by Priscus the Proconsul of Asia, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, after they had overcome bonds and beasts then they saluted one another with an holy kiss, and gave up their souls in prayer to God.
<h>L</h>ikewise the holy martyrs Apellius, Luke, and Clement, (who were among the first disciples of the Lord Christ.)
<h>I</h>n Bithynia, the holy sisters Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora, Virgins, who passed into glory crowned with martyrdom, under Maximian the Emperor and Fronto the President.
<h>A</h>t Compostella, holy Bishop Peter, famous for many graces and miracles.
<h>I</h>n the city of Albi, in Gaul, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Salvius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Novara, (in the sixth century,) holy Agapius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, (in the fifth century,) the holy Virgin Pulcheria, Empress of the Romans, famous for godliness.
<h>A</h>t Naples, in Campania, (in the sixth century,) holy Candida, called the Younger, famous for miracles.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
